Brain implants and the fear of thought crimes shape this Joe Rogan Experience segment on the wired future. Companies like Neuralink are putting chips in human brains to help paralyzed people control machines. Rogan and his guest look past the medical promise to the darker uses.

They ask what happens when tech can read signals close to thoughts themselves. Privacy of mind, ads in dreams, and state access to inner life all come up. The guest weighs real near-term science against science fiction. For the wary, the segment maps a future where the last private place may be opened.
uslaw-usc-t2-s661e:
Section 661e of Title 2 of the United States Code carves the big federal insurance programs out of credit reform. The credit reform subchapter sets rules for counting the cost of loans and guarantees. This section declares that it shall not apply to a named set of activities.

The excluded list reads like a roll of the government's insurers. The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation heads it, guarding bank deposits. The National Credit Union Administration and the Resolution Trust Corporation follow. The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation, which backstops private pensions, is named as well. National Flood Insurance and Crop Insurance are excluded in the same breath. The Tennessee Valley Authority closes the list. A study duty follows in the text, joining the two budget directors. The carve-out keeps giant insurance funds under their own accounting rather than the loan rules.
